4723943970104476939.String:
When the Angels of the Tenth Realm, Heven, waged war on Asgard, Odin's daughter and heir to Asgard's throne was kidnapped by the Queen of Angels. But Odin would not be extorted by the Angels, and his daughter, Aldrif, was seemingly slain. Odin retaliated by severing Heven from Yggdrasil and closed it off from the other Nine Realms. While sealed away, Aldrif was discovered to have survived and was then raised—hidden from her true heritage—as Angela, Huntress of Heven.

As all secrets eventually come to light, Angela uncovered the truth of her upbringing. Now, shunned from Heven and branded a traitor to Asgard, Angela roams across the realms to find her place within it—continuing her hunt wherever it takes her.

The Age of Ultron is upon us. Enter Central Park with four other players and battle Ultron and his army of deadly sentries. This is no walk in the park.

Even though Alpha Flight was not strictly a team of mutants, the group still had ties to the history of the X-Men. Wolverine even briefly led the team, before he had a...falling out with Department H, the section of the Canadian government tasked with oversight of all superhuman programs.

One of Alpha Flight's earliest missions brought us into direct conflict with the X-Men, when we attempt to return Wolverine to the service of Department H. We weren't up to the task, and it took some time before our two teams overcame the bad blood created by that encounter.

In addition to myself and my sister Aurora, Alpha Flight and its various subteams included mutants such as Madison Jeffries, Diamond Lil, Flashback, Windshear, Flex, Radius, and Wild Child.

That is quite a lot of mutants, but even so we were never anything but a minority on the team. If you truly would learn of other teams of mutant superhumans, you should speak to #mission#Magik#/mission# about her comrades on the New Mutants.

5320153544733230398.String:
Through Abigail Brand's intel in Fury's Toolshed, you were tasked with heading back to Hell's Kitchen to uncover a potential Skrull invasion force.

Once you arrived, you were successful in locating a group of civilians that were surrounded by Skrulls posing as street punks and thugs. You rescued them, and they were more than willing to give you some information about the location of some possible Skrull commanders.

You continued further into the area and tracked down the source of the Skrull invasion: Skrull commanders posing as heroes! A challenging battle began while you dealt with the Skrull versions of Iron Fist, Luke Cage, and Punisher.

5321261873934828870.String:
If you'd asked me a few years back, I'd have told you there was no way I'd ever be an Avenger.

The issues they deal with—intergalactic wars, time-travelling despots, indestructible killer robots—those just seemed like problems way outside my area of expertise. 

But when my good buddy Luke Cage joined, I started realizing that the Avengers needed heroes with both feet still on the ground. I may have grown up in a mystical Kung Fu city hidden in the Himalayas, but I've spent enough time fighting street crimes that I understand what it's like down on Earth. I guess that's why it's good to have folks like Luke, Daredevil, Spider-Man, and me around.

Plus, the Avengers have often been a little light on mystical expertise, so I like to think my spiritual side adds a useful spice to the team dynamic. Because when you're fighting off a demonic invasion, it's useful to have a guy around who understands interdimensional politics.

I hope that's helpful. Tell #mission#Ben Urich#/mission# I wish him good luck with his story, and let him know that when he's ready to write a big feature on the local martial arts scene I'm around to talk.

5806307258111296833.String:
Psylocke sure loves to talk about ancient history, don't she? Well, listen close and I'll fill you in on stuff that's a little bit more important to us here today.

The Professor was one of the first people to hold the idea that mutants and humans might be able to get along rather than just fighting each other. He did his best to recruit other mutants to his cause, and set up the private school we're standin' in to house those early X-Men. 

He even trained his students to protect normal humans from danger, and for a little while folks regarded the X-Men as heroes. But the good times didn't last, and soon people started speakin' up against Xavier's dream of peaceful co-existence between humans and mutants. 

People like #emphasis#Bolivar Trask#/emphasis#, who invented the Sentinel robots for the government to hunt down mutants.

People like #emphasis#William Stryker#/emphasis#, founder of the Purification Crusade that says mutants are an abomination in God's eyes.

And even people like the Professor's former friend Erik Lehnsherr, who started callin' himself #emphasis#Magneto#/emphasis# and recruited a team of mutants to fight against both the humans AND the X-Men. Sad to say, I actually belonged to one o' those evil mutant teams before the X-Men took me in.

The lines were drawn. Humans on one side, afraid of these strange new people with scary powers. An' mutants on the other, with some tryin' to make a difference—good or bad—and all of 'em just tryin' to survive.

You better go chat with #mission#Professor X#/mission# before all this gets me depressed.

#emphasis#The Hammerhead Gang#/emphasis#, huh? Yeah, as an Assistant District Attorney I had plenty of courtroom encounters with those guys.

The Hammerhead Gang is a massive crime syndicate. Normally they're divided up into rival families, but recently they were united under the rule of one man: Wilson Fisk, the so-called #emphasis#Kingpin of Crime#/emphasis#.

This Kingpin is a piece of work and virtually untouchable. Nobody can prove any of his crimes, and he's got half the cops and judges in the city either on his payroll or terrified of him. With the Hammerhead Gang on his side he also has the firepower to stand up against anyone crazy enough to threaten his position.

I'm getting angry just talking about this guy. Good thing I have a little more self-control than my cousin, huh?

Hey, good luck against the Hammerheads and the Kingpin. I don't envy you what you're up against.

6087967146045932860.String:
So you're helping Dani with her lesson plan? Of course I'm happy to chat with you.

Some people believe that mutants are a new presence in the world, but the opposite its true. The origin of mutankind, or Homo Sapiens Superior as some call us, dates back to long before recorded history begins.

In the very distant past, a supremely powerful group of aliens called the #emphasis#Celestials#/emphasis# visited Earth. During their experiments upon local life forms, the Celestials implanted a strand of DNA that would occasionally result in strange mutations in certain humans. Some mutations were merely minor physical aberrations from the norm, but others took the form of uncanny abilities or super powers. Regardless, those who manifested in this way were known as mutants.

For thousands of years, very few mutants made their presence known. Two of the the earliest recorded mutants are among the X-Men's most feared enemies: the immortal witch #emphasis#Selene#/emphasis# and the would-be world conqueror known as #emphasis#Apocalypse#/emphasis#.

During the 20th century, the mutant population grew exponentially. This growth drew the attention of many individuals, from our own Professor Xavier to villains such as the #emphasis#Shadow King#/emphasis# and #emphasis#Mister Sinister#/emphasis#.

The word mutant hadn't yet become a household word, but it was close. The stage was set for a grand conflict over the future of mutantkind...which I'm sure #mission#Rogue#/mission# can tell you more about.

After a tragic event while serving overseas, Flash agreed to an experiment that would subject him to the Venom Symbiote in order to become a new breed of super soldier. 6168735346156242304.String:
So Dani has you researching mutant superteams, huh? Sure, I guess I can give you a primer on the first and BEST team of mutants that didn't bear the name X-Men.

A few years back, it looked like the X-Men had died in space fighting the alien Brood. Professor Xavier almost gave up on his school, and it took some convincing from #emphasis#Moira MacTaggert#/emphasis# to talk him into gathering another class of young mutants.

He recruited five young mutants—Karma, Wolfsbane, Sunspot, Cannonball, and Psyche (Dani's first super hero identity)—and vowed that he would train them not for combat but simply on how best to live with their powers.

Of course, that didn't last long. Soon the team was getting into crazy adventures all over the world, including fights with the #emphasis#Hellfire Club#/emphasis#, the immortal mutant witch #emphasis#Selene#/emphasis#, and cybernetic aliens from outer space called the #emphasis#Technarchy#/emphasis#.

I joined the team not long after escaping from the hell dimension of Limbo, and other early recruits included Magma, Cypher, and Warlock. Professor Xavier even tried to demote my friend Kitty Pryde from the X-Men to our team! You can guess how well that went over with her.

In addition to new members, we also went through team leaders. In what must qualify as one of the all-time most boneheaded decision, Xavier once appointed Magneto to run the school and oversee our team in his absence! 

Then came the day when Cable showed up, and everything about the team changed. Even the group's name changed...but to learn about X-Force you ought to talk with #mission#Psylocke#/mission#.

#emphasis#Real Name:#/emphasis# Victor von Doom
#emphasis#Identity:#/emphasis# Public

Victor von Doom has not lived an easy life. Born in Latveria, Victor's mother was claimed by the demon Mephisto in a mystical deal gone wrong. The loss of his mother would be Victor's key motivating force, driving him to excel in the study of any way to free her from Mephisto's grasp: scientific or mystical. His studies would eventually bring him to New York State University alongside Reed Richards and Ben Grimm. Building a machine to save his mother, Victor was caught in the ensuing explosion that Reed Richards warned would happen. Expelled and with his face disfigured, Victor von Doom would eternally blame the future Mister Fantastic for his own failures. Even taking over his homeland of Latveria in order to utilize its resources for his schemes was not enough for Doom. Only the humiliation of cursed Richards and total global domination will sate the appetite of Doctor Doom!
 
#emphasis#Created By:#/emphasis# Stan Lee and Jack Kirby

6470096442277758272.String:
You say you're going up against #emphasis#HYDRA#/emphasis#? I feel sorry for you.

HYDRA is a fascist organization whose origin dates back to World War II (or maybe much earlier, depending on which stories you believe). Their goal is simple: world domination. These guys actually believe that we'd all be better off if their "enlightened rulers" ran everything.

Thankfully, there are folks like you and me—and the dedicated agents of S.H.I.E.L.D.—who think differently.

HYDRA has employed a lot of infamous villains over the years. For a while they even had me under their thumb, but thankfully Nick Fury helped get me out of there.

The most prominent face of the organization is a psychotic woman named Viper, who holds the rank of #emphasis#Madame HYDRA#/emphasis#. Some people think she's actually just a field general working for a higher-ranking leader, but nobody knows who that might be.

If HYDRA is active in Madripoor, they must think something important is hidden there. They wouldn't go up against the Hand without a good reason.

#emphasis#Real Name:#/emphasis# Alex Summers
#emphasis#Identity:#/emphasis# Public

Alex Summers, better known as Havok, is a powerful mutant capable of absorbing cosmic energy and releasing it in devastating bursts.

A longtime member of the X-Men and a leader in his own right, Havok has fought alongside his fellow mutants through countless battles and crises, even leading teams of his own. Often living in the shadow of his legendary brother Cyclops, Alex has nevertheless forged his own identity as a hero, determined to prove that he is more than his family’s legacy—or the danger of his own abilities.

Though his path has taken him from Earth to the far reaches of the cosmos and back, Alex Summers continues to turn the power he once feared into a weapon against those who threaten mutantkind.

#emphasis#Created By:#/emphasis# Don Heck and Arnold Drake

#listheader#MARVEL HEROES BASIC COMMANDS#/listheader#
Move: $PrimaryActionButtonPressed$ on open ground.
Activate Power: $PrimaryActionButtonPressed$, $SecondaryActionButtonPressed$, $PowerButtonPressed 2$, $PowerButtonPressed 3$, $PowerButtonPressed 4$, $PowerButtonPressed 5$, $PowerButtonPressed 6$, or $PowerButtonPressed 7$.
(To stand in place while using powers, hold down SHIFT.)
Activate Ultimate Power: $DedicatedUltimateSlotPressed$ (once unlocked)
Activate your Travel Power: $TravelPowerButtonPressed$ (can be toggled)
Activate your Med Kit: $DedicatedHealSlotPressed$
Close UI Windows: $MarvelGFxHandleEscapePress$ or $MarvelGFxCloseAllPanels$
View Help Screens: $MarvelGFxHandleEscapePress$, then select Help.
View Options: $MarvelGFxHandleEscapePress$, then select Options.
Quit Game: $MarvelGFxHandleEscapePress$, then select Quit.

#listheader#INTERACTIONS AND CHAT COMMANDS#/listheader#
Interact with NPC: $PrimaryActionButtonPressed$ on NPC.
Invite Player to Team: CTRL + $PrimaryActionButtonPressed$ on player's hero; OR type #emphasis#/partyinvite [HeroName]#/emphasis#.
Leave Your Team: Type #emphasis#/partyleave#/emphasis#.
/ignore: Adds a player to your ignore list. Type as #emphasis#/ignore [HeroName]#/emphasis#.
/party: Sends message to the #emphasis#team#/emphasis# chat channel, allowing only your teammates to see it.
/guild: Sends a message to the #emphasis#supergroup#/emphasis# chat channel, allowing only your supergroup members to see it.
/say: Sends message to the default (#emphasis#local#/emphasis#) chat channel, allowing all nearby players to see it.
/tell: Sends a private message to another player. Type as #emphasis#/tell [HeroName] [message]#/emphasis#, replacing the bracketed entries with the appropriate text.

#listheader#INVENTORY, LOOT, AND VENDORS#/listheader#
View Inventory: I
Reveal Loot on Ground: $RevealInteractiblesToggle$
Slot Item: $SecondaryActionButtonPressed$ on item in Inventory.
Buy Item from Vendor: $SecondaryActionButtonPressed$ on item icon in vendor window.
Sell Item to Vendor: $SecondaryActionButtonPressed$ on item icon in Inventory (when vendor window is open).
Advance Vendor or Crafter Rank: $RevealInteractiblesToggle$ + $SecondaryActionButtonPressed$ on item icon in Inventory (when vendor window is open).

#listheader#COSTUMES#/listheader#
Find new costumes for your heroes as loot or by purchasing them from the store (press X to visit the store).
Upgrade your costumes at any #emphasis#crafter#/emphasis#.


#listheader#POWERS#/listheader#
View Power Trees: $MarvelGFxGameUITogglePanel PowerLibraryPanel$
Assign Power: Drag power icon from its #emphasis#power tree#/emphasis# into your HUD.


#listheader#CHARACTER MANAGEMENT#/listheader#
View Character Sheet: $MarvelGFxGameUITogglePanel CharacterSheetPanel$
Slot Item: $SecondaryActionButtonPressed$ on item in Inventory.
View Hero Roster: $MarvelGFxGameUITogglePanel RosterPanel$
Switch Active Hero: In Hero Roster, $PrimaryActionButtonPressed$ on new hero's portrait then $PrimaryActionButtonPressed$ SWITCH.


Unlock New Hero: Press $MarvelGFxGameUITogglePanel StorePanel$ to visit the store, or collect #emphasis#eternity splinters#/emphasis# and visit Adam Warlock in any base.


#listheader#MISSIONS, MINI-MAP, AND TRAVEL#/listheader#
Open Mission Log: $MarvelGFxGameUITogglePanel MissionLogPanel$
View Mission Objectives: In Mission Log, $PrimaryActionButtonPressed$ on mission in the left pane.
Toggle Map Mode: $ToggleMiniMapMode$ switches between the mini-map in the corner of your screen and a full-screen map mode.
Zoom Out Mini-Map: "-" on the mini-map.
Zoom In Mini-Map: "+" on the mini-map
Scroll Full-Screen Map: Use arrow keys to scroll up, down, left, or right.
Use Portal or Waypoint: $PrimaryActionButtonPressed$ on portal or waypoint.
Activate Bodyslider: Click on the Bodyslider button at the upper right of your screen (it looks like a house). This returns you to the last base you visited. Clicking it again brings you back to where you were when you activated it the first time. "B" will also activate your Bodyslider.

7441935318163850563.String:
Welcome to the Danger Room.

The Danger Room is near limitless in the forms it can take. For now, I'll leave it in its powered-off state for the purposes of this training demonstration.

I'm going to cover a few things that you will undoubtedly encounter during the course of a Danger Room scenario. First, in order to complete a given scenario you must complete several challenges. To complete a challenge you must fill the Progression Bar that will appear on your HUD. This can be done in one of two ways. Let's review the first method.

7786525895790560526.String:
Salutations, $AvatarName$. 

Need a refresher?

The area you are in now is the launching pad for all of the training simulations you will be running. Bring your Scenario Chips here and activate them to get started. Activating one will destroy the chip in the process and create a portal to your Scenario. Don't fret, Danger Room Scenarios are designed to be ran frequently so there are plenty of Chips out there for you to find and experience.

Scenarios are designed to be a challenge. As you will find, each Scenario Chip has data stored upon it that will dictate what sort of challenges you will face. Very few Scenarios will run the same. Your Scenario's data can be viewed on the Chip itself before you activate it, on the created Scenario's portal itself, and, lastly, as a reminder when you're running the Scenario, in your Mission Tracker panel.

Learn by doing, $AvatarName$. The most efficient way to learn Danger Room is to continue to run Scenarios.

That about covers the basics. Make use of the resources available to you here in the Danger Room and best of luck to you on your training.

Hello there, hero. Director Fury sent me to instruct you on the use of your #emphasis#Bodyslider#/emphasis# device.

Your Bodyslider is a personal teleportation device designed to get you to a nearby safe place. Our eggheads in R&D assure me it was tested extensively.

To activate the device, click the Bodyslider button in your HUD. It's the icon that looks like a house, located next to your mini-map.

When activated, your Bodyslider returns you (and only you) back to the last base you visited. This allows you to visit vendors, talk to your mission contacts, or just catch your breath. The portal remains, allowing you to return quickly to the exact place where you activated it.

After you activate your Bodyslider, it takes seven minutes to recharge it, so use it wisely.

7942232573597320519.String:
#orange#Welcome to the Shared Quest System!#/orange#
- These are super-sized quests that are automatically shared with all players, allowing them to be seamlessly completed by groups or individuals, regardless of level, group status, or location.

- All players receive the same Shared Quests each day. New ones are assigned every day, generally including a Midtown Patrol quest, a quest to defeat threats in Terminals and a quest in X-Defense or S.H.I.E.L.D. Holo-Sim.

- Three Shared Quests exist each day. You may complete any of them any number of times. As soon as you complete a Shared Quest, you will immediately begin earning progress towards the next one. Shared Quests may be completed alongside or in place of Legendary Quests, sharing credit at all times.

- Rewards for Quests include Odin Marks, credits, experience orbs and random gear of all-  possible rarities and types, based on the difficulty of the Shared Quest.

- The first time you complete each of the Shared Quests, each day, you will receive bonus rewards, including a bonus Infinity Orb.

Rogue told you to come talk to me about the #emphasis#Morlocks#/emphasis#? Well I'm no expert, but I've heard some stories from my friend Kitty Pryde, so I guess I'll have to do.

A few decades back, a group of mutant outcasts decided to leave society behind. They moved into some old tunnels beneath New York City and started calling themselves the Morlocks. Some of these tunnels ran for miles and miles, if you can believe that.

The Morlocks basically became a street gang that lived under the streets, coming up at night to steal what they needed to live. The X-Men had a few run-ins with them, but eventually we called a truce. The mutants that live down there now are basically peaceful.

Y'know, if the Purifiers are causing trouble in Mutant Town, it's a good bet the Morlocks are getting hit pretty bad too. I hope you can help them out a little.

The goal of a Rorschach test is to provide data about a S.H.I.E.L.D. agent's cognition and personality variables such as motivations, response tendencies, cognitive operations, affectivity, and personal/interpersonal perceptions. The assumption is that an agent will class external stimuli based on person-specific perceptual sets and that this clustering process is representative of the process used during actual high-risk and combat situations in the field.

Using these test results, S.H.I.E.L.D. psychologists, working with veteran tacticians and field officers, have developed a system of personalized training dubbed "Combat Rorschach" that allows agents to perceive and analyze situations from many angles simultaneously, giving them a tremendous advantage in combat operations.

#emphasis#Magneto#/emphasis# formed the first version of the Brotherhood of Mutants back in the early days of the X-Men. It included Toad, Mastermind, and two mutants who didn't know at the time that he was their father: Quicksilver and the Scarlet Witch. 

The Brotherhood tangled with the X-Men on a number of occasions, including once when Magneto actually tried taking over the tiny nation of Santo Marco. After Quicksilver and the Scarlet Witch left to join the Avengers, Magneto recruited others to his team, including Blob, Lorelei, and Unus the Untouchable.

In what must rank as the saddest chapter of the Brotherhood, Magneto gathered together a collection of third-rate mutant villains for yet another scheme: Burner, Lifter, Peeper, Slither, and Shocker (not the two-bit thug running around Manhattan, mind you, but someone even less competent). Thankfully, Magneto had the good taste to abandon this group shortly after gathering them.

The next generation of the Brotherhood was spearheaded by the shapechanger Mystique. To learn more about her collections of mutant villains, you should speak with #mission#Rogue#/mission#, here at Xavier's School.

#listheader#Entering Fire and Ice PvP#/listheader#
After reaching level 20 #mission#left-click any #/mission# a #emphasis#waypoint#/emphasis# to access the M.A.P.  On the #emphasis#Challenge#/emphasis# tab, choose Fire & Ice PvP. 

Once you confirm the waypoint, you'll enter a queue while the game looks for other players for you to play PvP with. You're free to do whatever you like while you're in the queue. 

When you're notified that a game has been found, #mission#left-click#/mission# on the orange queue icon on the top right, then #mission#left-click#/mission# OK to enter the match.

#red#Level Tiers#/red# 
PvP matches are broken up into level tiers to help ensure that matches are between players near each other's level.  The tiers are:
- Tier 1: Level 20-29
- Tier 2: Level 30-39
- Tier 3: Level 40-49
- Tier 4: Level 50-59
- Tier 5: Level 60

Players who are below the max level for a level band receive some bonuses to help them compete.

#red#Entering PvP With A Party#/red# 
You can enter the PvP queue with your party, and you are guaranteed to be on a team with your party members as long as you're all in the same level band.


#listheader#Dealing with DEFENDERS#/listheader#
Your PvP faction has six defenders and one guardian. Protect them! You lose the match if all seven are destroyed.

Battles often center around defenders, and destroying one is a big step towards winning the match.

#red#Tip! Deadly Defenders#/red#
Defenders are very dangerous and can defeat any hero with only a few shots, so don't take one on by yourself!

#red#Tip! Defender Targeting#/red#
Defenders will target the first enemy that gets into range, and continue to attack that target until it is destroyed. Attacking the defender won't change its target, but if you attack an enemy hero near one of their defenders, the 
defender will immediately target you!

#red#Tip! Defeat Defenders In Order#/red#
You must defeat the defenders in the order you find them.  Only the closest defenders can take damage - the rest are invincible!

#listheader#Fight Alongside Your GOLEMS#/listheader#
Each team's base spawns #emphasis#golems#/emphasis# at regular intervals. These golems move straight down the path, attacking any enemy target they see, whether it is a hero, defender, or another golem.

#red#Tip! Stay With Your Golems#/red#
Let your golems take the brunt of the damage from enemies while you focus on more important targets.  This is especially true when attacking the powerful defenders. Let the defender target one of your golems, then attack it while its 
distracted.


#listheader#GLYPHSTONES and GLYPHS#/listheader#
Defeated golems and enemy heroes drop #emphasis#glyphstones#/emphasis#. You can trade glyphstones to vendors back at your base for #emphasis#glyphs#/emphasis#, which provide a buff that last for the entire match, even if you are defeated.  

There are a wide variety of glyph effects, such as increasing your health, increasing your speed, or improving your critical chance. Purchase glyphs whenever you can!

#red#Tip! Stacking Glyphs#/red#
Most glyphs stack, meaning you can purchase them multiple times to increase their effectiveness.  A glyph's price increases with each successive purchase, however.


#listheader#DEFEAT and RESPAWNING#/listheader#
If you are defeated in a PvP match, you can wait to be revived by a teammate, but that's not always possible.  If you choose to respawn, you'll immediately appear back at base, but you'll be unable to move for for a short duration.  The 
longer the match has progressed, the longer you'll have to wait.

While you're waiting, it's a great time to buy runes from the vendors.  


#listheader#PvP REWARDS#/listheader#
When a PvP match ends, you receive a mission to talk to Sif in Asgard.  She'll reward you with XP, eternity splinters, and items, with the match's winning team getting the best items.

#red#Tip! Golden Crowns#/red#
You also get a #emphasis#golden crown#/emphasis# as part of your PvP reward.  Collect golden crowns and trade them to Valkyrie for #emphasis#rings#/emphasis#, that are designed to be particularly useful for PvP.

You can find Valkryie in Asgard.


#listheader#General PvP RULES#/listheader#
- Check out your lifetime PvP Victory and Defeat stats on the Character Screen (Press #mission#C#/mission#)
- Being defeated in PvP has no negative ramifications. For example, defeats in PvP do not add to your "Defeats" total found on the character screen, and they do not reduce the power of Bloodstone Totem artifacts.
- There is no friendly fire. You cannot harm anyone on your faction.
- Item Invulnerability powers have a 1.5 minute cooldown in PvP.


#listheader#Leaving PvP#/listheader#
When a PvP match is over, you automatically return to Asgard.
